root.claim: The integer product is computed exactly on one fixed-tape machine in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time.
root.method: reduce exact multiplication to convolution of radix digits, compute the convolution by synthetic transforms on tape layouts, and bound the total tape cost with a power saving

motivation.text: The reduction is exact, so only its cost needs bounding; each tape procedure costs a power of its width below linear, and the parameters are chosen so that this saving survives every layer.

children.claim: Each prime-length Fourier transform is expressed through a tensor transform with power-of-two axis lengths, keeping the source and target permutations inside the identity.
children.method: Gaussian resampling, computing the transform formula directly with both permutations retained

motivation.text:
The transform lengths needed for the integer product are pairwise coprime,
whereas the synthetic transforms use powers of two. Gaussian resampling
connects these two shapes.

children.claim: Normalized cyclic convolution on the power-of-two axes is computed over the polynomial ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ by synthetic transforms and packed polynomial products.
children.method: phase twist of the last coordinate into the polynomial ring, synthetic transforms on retained layouts, pointwise product, then signed packing with the established multiplier

motivation.text: Powers of the polynomial variable act as roots of unity, and multiplying by such a root is a signed shift, so the transforms need only shifts and butterflies.

children.claim: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, and its negative wrap gives the original cyclic wrap.

quote.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic
wrap after the twist is removed.

children.claim: The two forward synthetic transforms keep the same frequency order through their pointwise product, which the opposite transform consumes.

children.claim: Polynomial products are computed by signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier used as a subroutine.

quote.quote:
Their polynomial products
use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an

children.claim: The recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, so rounding and carry propagation give the exact binary product.

quote.quote:
Section~\ref{sec:assembly} removes
the known normalizations and digit scales, proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product.

children.claim: The tape operations of the algorithm cost $O(V(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ in total, for stored volume $V=\Theta(n)$.
children.method: bound the cost of each tape procedure by a fixed power of its width below linear, then choose compatible fixed rational parameters

motivation.text: The reduction is exact, so only its cost needs bounding; each tape procedure costs a power of its width below linear, and the parameters are chosen so that this saving survives every layer.

children.claim: Interchanging two equal address fields of width $u$ costs less than linear in $u$ per unit volume.
children.method: rank-saving recursion on a bit network whose smaller calls have total rank below the number of wires times the parameter

motivation.text:
Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times
$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

quote.quote:
An edge matrix of rank $a$ will require $a$ smaller interchanges.
Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times
$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.
